thread:
jun: Quick heads-up — seeing a 95th+ latency tail on hosted when routing to flash+paged fused kernels under our continuous-batching path. Not wide spread but reproducible on a 2k qps steady workload. :thinking:

maria: ack. timeline? any change in traffic or model variants around the time this started?

jun: started ~3h ago after the scheduler bump that increased max batch window from 12->18ms. No model change. Only noticed on long-prefill -> small decode flows (seq_prefill ~512, decode steps short).

sam: can you dump a perf record / nvprof of one of the slow decode invocations? also kv cache behavior?

jun: pasted a quick flame dump from perf (stripped). looks like fused attention kernel hangs around longer, and we see a burst of L2 misses during the KVCACHE load phase:

```
# jun@host: perf top snippet
50.1% fused_flash_paged_kernel
18.2% kvcache_load_page
  - L2_MISS: 1.3e6
  - DRAM_LAT: 120us
8.7% cudaMemcpyAsync (small)
5.0% scheduler_wait
```

nate: that L2 miss number looks huge for small decode. are pages thrashing because prefill left big KV footprint then decode accesses sparse keys?

jun: exactly hypothesis — prefill writes contiguous KV pages; small decode probes a handful of keys across many heads, causing many page loads. The fused kernel touches KV in a way that serializes page fetches.

maria: can you run a targeted bench? compare fused-flash vs separated flash+kv-prefetch for small decode microbatches. bench-bot: @bench-bot run quick-small-decode-sweep( model=redwood-base, seq_prefill=512, decode_len=8, qps=250, duration=2m ) :rocket:

bench-bot: scheduled. results in ~45s.

bench-bot: results:
- fused_flash_paged: p50=22ms p95=148ms p99=315ms
- flash_separated_prefetch: p50=20ms p95=65ms p99=92ms
- flash_paged_no_fuse: p50=21ms p95=78ms p99=105ms

sam: big delta on p95/p99 for fused. that's the tail. what about GPU occupancy and SM stalls?

jun: occupancy snapshot (per-kernel): fused_flash_paged occupancy 0.48, warp_stalls_mem 62%, memory_throughput spiky. separated path occupancy 0.71, warp_stalls_mem 34%. Looks like fused path is memory serializing, underutilizing compute.

maria: interesting. Could be because fused kernel iterates per-head and triggers page faults for each head instead of aggregating KV page accesses. We added an optimization to touch per-page once, but scheduler window increase means more outstanding MPs so the fusion path loses locality.

nate: any quick mitigations? options:
- revert kernel fuse for decode path
- add micro-prefetch stage before fused execute (batch-local aggregation of page IDs)
- reduce max batch window back to 12ms

sam: try prefetch aggregation first — cheap and might keep fused benefits for prefill while avoiding thrash for small decode. we can implement a path that, during decode for small batches, scans KV access indices and issues batch-prefetch async copies in parallel, then run fused kernel.

jun: implemented prototype in runtime: call gather_kv_pages(batch) -> cudaMemcpyAsync for unique pages -> cudaStreamSynchronize before fused kernel. Quick smoke shows p95 drop from 148ms -> 72ms, p99 315 -> 110ms. p50 unchanged.

maria: good. what's CPU overhead? any extra latency for prefetch sync?
jun: prefetch sync adds ~4ms on average but we save on large stalls so net wins on tail. Also memory copy sizes are small (a few pages).

sam: can we make it conditional? heuristic: if decode_batch_size <= 4 && decode_len <= 16 && unique_kv_pages > threshold then prefetch, else normal path. Also expose flag in runtime to A/B test.

maria: agree. Also add telemetry: emit kvcache_prefetch{triggered:true/false}, prefetch_pages, prefetch_latency, post_kernel_dram_wait. So we can correlate.

nate: we should still consider long term: kernel design that aggregates page loads inside kernel (cooperative loads) might avoid CPU prefetch, but it's complex. For now prefetched async copy + cheap heuristic is good ship candidate.

jun: opened PR: runtime/prefetcher: add decode-prefetch-heuristic + flags. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823 (DRAFT).

maria: add a test that simulates worst-case sparse key access to avoid regressions. Also include a canary on dedicated that toggles flag off for 24h to validate nothing else regresses.

sam: thumbs. if bench-bot can run nightly sweep across model sizes + seq combos we can bake better thresholds. bench-bot: queued nightly-sweep(all_models, seq_prefill=[256,512,1024], decode_len=[8,16,32], batch_sizes=[1,2,4,8]).

bench-bot: queued. ETA 7h.

jun: TL;DR: tail regression caused by fused_flash_paged kernel interacting poorly with KV page loads under the new batching window. Short-term mitigation: prefetch aggregation for small decode, heuristic feature flag, telemetry. Long-term: revisit fusion logic to aggregate page loads in-kernel or change KV layout to reduce page count.

maria: thanks. can you post PR link when ready and assign to sam + nate for review? Also drop a short note in eng-runtime channel about the runtime flag and default (enabled for hosted for now).

jun: will do. posting PR now. (reaction :white_check_mark:)
